Hi all — attaching the artifacts Alex requested. Summary below and files attached.

Summary (high level):
- SCC mapping: matrix that maps each SCC clause to Redwood controls and evidence (see redwood_scc_mapping_20260609.xlsx). Rows include: data categories, lawful basis, subprocessor controls, SCC clause ref.
- Data flow diagram: simplified diagram showing Hosted API path, optional Dedicated hop, and US-based asynchronous analytics pipeline (see redwood_data_flow_diagram_20260609.png).
- KMS & keys: we use AWS KMS for Hosted and Dedicated by default; for Private deployments customers can provide their own KMS (BYOK). We rotate asymmetric signing keys annually and symmetric data encryption keys rotate automatically every 90 days. (See redwood_kms_and_keys_summary_20260609.pdf)
- Encryption specifics: TLS 1.2+ for in-transit; AES-256-GCM for at-rest object stores; token-level encryption for sensitive blobs where applicable.
- Subprocessors: primary cloud providers (AWS eu-west-1, GCP europe-west3) and CDN provider (FastEdge); full subprocessor list is in the SCC mapping worksheet.
- Logging/retention: request logs retained 30 days by default for Hosted; configurable for Dedicated. Audit-export: logs can be exported to a customer-controlled bucket for up to 12 months on request.

Notes / caveats:
- The diagram highlights an optional US analytics pipeline that runs de-identified aggregates for service reliability — raw PII is not sent to that pipeline unless explicitly enabled by the customer.
- Private (on-prem/VPC) customers can pin region/disable cross-border replication.

Attachments: 3 files (listed below).

Files attached (stubs):
- redwood_scc_mapping_20260609.xlsx (spreadsheet)
- redwood_kms_and_keys_summary_20260609.pdf (pdf)
- redwood_data_flow_diagram_20260609.png (image)

If you'd like, Rishi can add a short engineering note on how KV cache and prefix caching are retained in-memory only and never written to durable object storage without customer opt-in.

Best,
